title: The quasi-coherator counit on a flat scheme test
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal Z/S$ an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], with its ringed big fppf site [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] and module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $H$ be locally quasi-coherent and flat-compatible in the explicit sense of [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator], and let $q_H:j_{\mathcal Z}Q_{\mathcal Z}H\to H$ be the counit of that node. For a scheme test $z:T\to\mathcal Z$ which is flat on scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism], restriction of $q_H$ to the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_T$-module sheaves. In particular its value $q_H(z):(Q_{\mathcal Z}H)(z)\to H(z)$ is an isomorphism. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis on $\mathcal Z$, $z$, or $H$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GQK, lemma-flat-object-and-Q, statement and proof (the notation is the locally quasi-coherent flat-base-change category of lemma-adjoint).

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:U\to\mathcal Z$ using [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Its relation $R=U\times_{\mathcal Z}U$ and triple relation are algebraic spaces by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Their projections are smooth, hence flat, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Put $N=H_U$, a quasi-coherent etale module by [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator]. On each etale scheme chart $V\to R$, the two maps $v_i:V\to U$ are flat. The two objects $av_1,av_2$ are isomorphic by the defining $2$-arrow of $R$. Their restrictions identify the targets of the flat-comparison isomorphisms $c_i:v_i^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{av_i}$. Define $\delta_V=c_2^{-1}c_1:v_1^*N\to v_2^*N$. These maps and their inverses commute with etale chart restrictions: on a local tensor $b\otimes m$ each comparison is $b$ times the restriction of $m$, so composing comparisons is the comparison for the composite arrow. The etale scheme charts of $R$ form a jointly surjective etale family, hence an fppf covering by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus](1), so full faithfulness of descent in [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] glues them to an isomorphism $\delta:p_1^*N\simeq p_2^*N$ on $R$ (pullbacks as in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]). On a chart of the triple relation, $\delta_{23}\delta_{12}=c_3^{-1}c_2c_2^{-1}c_1=c_3^{-1}c_1=\delta_{13}$ under the tensor composition identifications; the identity comparison gives $e^*\delta=1$. The same faithfulness verifies these equalities globally.

source.place: Tag 0778, lemma-adjoint, construction of the groupoid datum; Tag 0779, lemma-adjoint-kernel-parasitic, atlas choice.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-module-descent] to $(N,\delta)$. Obtain $M\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)$ and an isomorphism $\eta:M_U\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ respecting the descent datum. The condition on $\eta$ is exactly $c_1^H p_1^*\eta=c_2^H p_2^*\eta\delta_M$. Hence [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-quasicoherent-source-maps] extends $\eta$ uniquely to a module map $\phi:M\to H$. For every $A\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Z)$, these same two cited statements identify maps $A\to M$ with compatible maps $A_U\to N$, and identify the latter with maps $A\to H$. Under these identifications the bijection is $f\mapsto\phi f$, because its restriction is $\eta f_U$.

source.place: Tag 0778, lemma-adjoint, the two displayed Hom identifications; Tag 076S, lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent.

proof.text: The actual counit $q_H:QH\to H$ has the same universal property by [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator]. Obtain unique maps $b:M\to QH$ and $c:QH\to M$ with $q_H b=\phi$ and $\phi c=q_H$. Injectivity of composition with $\phi$ on maps $M\to M$ gives $cb=1_M$, since $\phi cb=q_H b=\phi$. Injectivity of composition with $q_H$ on maps $QH\to QH$ gives $bc=1_{QH}$, since $q_Hbc=\phi c=q_H$. Therefore $b$ is invertible. Restricting $q_Hb=\phi$ to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ gives $(q_H)_U b_U=\eta$. Thus $(q_H)_U=\eta b_U^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. This is a uniqueness argument for universal arrows, with both inverse equations written out; it uses the bijection proved in step 2, not a property of an unspecified construction of $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0778, lemma-adjoint, adjunction identification; Tag 0779, proof of (2), counit on the chosen atlas.

proof.text: For the given flat test $z:T\to\mathcal Z$, let $W=T\times_{\mathcal Z}U$ with projections $r:W\to T$ and $s:W\to U$. This is an algebraic space by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $v:V\to W$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Set $g=rv:V\to T$ and $h=sv:V\to U$. The projection $r$ is smooth surjective as a base change of the atlas, whereas $s$ is flat as a scheme base change of the assumed chartwise-flat map $z$. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $g$ is smooth surjective and $h$ is flat. The defining $2$-arrow of $W$ identifies the objects $zg$ and $ah$. No assertion that $W$ is a scheme, or that any atlas or projection is quasi-compact, is needed.

source.place: Tag 0779, lemma-adjoint-kernel-parasitic, square W=V times_X U; Tag 0GQK, lemma-flat-object-and-Q.

proof.text: For $E=j_{\mathcal Z}QH$ and $E=H$, let $c_g^E:g^*E_T\to E_{zg}$ and $c_h^E:h^*E_U\to E_{ah}$ be the tensor comparisons. For $H$ they are isomorphisms by flat compatibility in [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator], since $g,h$ are flat. For $j_{\mathcal Z}QH$ they are isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction]. Naturality follows on local tensors $b\otimes m$ from the identity $q(b\,m|)=b\,q(m)|$. Consequently, after the identification $zg\simeq ah$, $$c_g^H\circ g^*(q_H)_T\circ(c_g^{jQH})^{-1}=q_{H,zg}=q_{H,ah}=c_h^H\circ h^*(q_H)_U\circ(c_h^{jQH})^{-1}.$$ The right side is an isomorphism by step 3, so $g^*(q_H)_T$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0779, proof of (1) and (2): the two flat-comparison identifications; Tag 0GQK.

proof.text: Both endpoints of $(q_H)_T$ are quasi-coherent etale modules: use [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] for $QH$ and the locally quasi-coherent hypothesis of [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator] for $H$. The singleton cover $g:V\to T$ is fppf by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus], since it is smooth surjective and hence flat locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Apply full faithfulness in [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] to this cover, viewing schemes as algebraic spaces. The inverse of $g^*(q_H)_T$ respects the two descent identifications: the compatibility equation for $g^*(q_H)_T$ can be multiplied on both sides by its inverse. It therefore descends to an inverse of $(q_H)_T$, and faithfulness verifies the two inverse equations. Thus the original restriction of the counit to $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0779, proof of (1): faithful pullback along the smooth surjection; Tag 0GQK, conclusion.

proof.text: Evaluate this isomorphism at the final object $1_T:T\to T$ of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By the definition of restriction along the test $z$, this evaluation is exactly $q_H(z):(QH)(z)\to H(z)$. Evaluating its inverse supplies the inverse on sections. All choices used only an arbitrary smooth atlas and etale charts; no finiteness or quasi-separatedness assumption has entered.

source.place: Tag 0GQK, lemma-flat-object-and-Q, evaluation at the test object.
